descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. This is a remote opportunity and we would be interested in applicants from Canadian EST time zones only.   Senior Software Engineer - Session Replay The Opportunity: The Session Replay squad is building a new Grafana Cloud product that helps our customers to understand what users actually experienced when something goes wrong. Session Replay connects frontend signals (errors, performance, synthetic checks) to concrete session-level evidence, enabling faster and more confident investigation of production issues. This team works at the intersection of: frontend observability, backend data processing and storage at scale, debugging workflows across products, privacy and access control, performance and cost constraints at scale. Session Replay is still early, which means you’ll help shape both what we build and how it fits into Grafana Cloud. A key part of our next phase is evolving the backend architecture of capturing sessions, including a migration toward columnar/analytical solution as a primary storage and query engine for high-volume session data. As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a new perspective to the software. We are looking for Senior Software Engineers who are passionate about working with data and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! Our stack is Golang, Typescript and React, but we build tools for people using many other stacks.  What You’ll Be Doing: As a Senior Software Engineer, you will operate as a technical leader and systems thinker, driving both product direction and architectural evolution, specifically, you will: Own end-to-end technical direction for Session Replay, spanning frontend, backend, and data systems Drive the evolution of our backend architecture, including: Designing systems around columnar/analytical data storage for large-scale session data   Defining data models, ingestion pipelines, and query patterns Lead the design of investigation workflows, connecting replay with logs, metrics, traces and other telemetry across Grafana Cloud Make high-leverage architectural decisions that impact multiple teams and products Partner with teams across Grafana (Frontend Observability, Synthetic Monitoring, Core Grafana) to build cohesive cross-product experiences Engage directly with customers - joining calls, gathering structured feedback, and helping customers instrument and adopt Session Replay successfully.  Improve engineering standards, patterns, and operational practices within the team Mentor engineers and help grow technical leadership within the team Technologies you'll work with: Go (backend services and APIs) Columnar/Analytical data storage (core data storage and querying) Object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob Storage) and MySQL  TypeScript / React (user-facing workflows) Grafana ecosystem (Mimir, Loki, Tempo, etc.) We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. What Makes You a Great Fit:  You are comfortable working in a remote-first company ; communication is key. For us, working together means being collaborative, friendly, kind, and respectful . We operate by consensus. You can contribute to a discussion, disagree constructively, and commit to the team’s decision. You are able to communicate design decisions clearly in written and spoken English. Ability to reason about data-intensive systems (ingestion, storage, querying, cost trade-offs) You are comfortable owning features in ambiguous problem spaces . We are a small team, working remotely, on a product that will be used by engineers all over the world – the ability to work on your own is crucial. You have a good understanding of a software development process that takes a user-centered approach . You easily build an understanding of the users’ context and goals which will help you build the right solution with the maximum value. You enjoy working on complex solutions – Grafana is a highly technological solution and has avid followers who rely on it every day and who care deeply about their work

These teams are changing how businesses operate, bringing AI into working life, and expanding access to its benefits. This work is central to our mission of ensuring AGI benefits all of humanity: helping people and businesses everywhere put AI to use in ways that improve their lives and livelihoods. We’re looking for someone with sharp editorial instincts, boundless creative ambition, and the sound judgment to handle sensitive, confidential, and consequential work with care. You should be equally comfortable setting the communications direction, writing an executive message that addresses what’s on employees’ minds directly and transparently, and hosting a live conversation that invites candid questions and open discussion. We’re looking for a pro who takes initiative, understands what matters to employees, and anticipates tough questions and pain points early enough to help leaders address them. This role can be based in San Francisco or New York City. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Keep work moving as priorities change. Move quickly, adapt as new information comes in, and keep everyone involved informed about decisions and next steps. Respond to feedback, adjust course without losing momentum, and bring a constructive, collaborative attitude to challenging moments. Strengthen the broader Internal Communications function. Contribute to shared priorities, provide thoughtful ideas and feedback, and turn successful approaches into practices others can use. You will thrive in this role if you have: 10+ years of relevant experience in internal or executive communications, marketing communications, operations, or a related field, with demonstrated ownership of complex communications programs. People Management experience (1-2 years minimum) is required. Experience advising senior leaders. You have built trust through preparation, discretion, and thoughtful and strategic recommendations, and can navigate disagreement with confidence and utmost respect. Excellent writing and editorial judgment. Curiosity about how businesses grow and how people use technology. You'll be the person who takes charge when something goes wrong. You'll lead investigations from first signal to root cause, coordinate containment across Security, SRE, and Engineering, and keep stakeholders informed while the incident is moving fast. This isn't a pure responder role. We want a well-rounded security engineer who has run real incidents and wants to make the next one faster. You'll write the scripts, automations, and tooling that take manual work out of triage, evidence collection, and containment. You'll also turn lessons from each incident into better detections, playbooks, and platform hardening. Responsibilities Incident Response Serve as incident commander or technical lead for security incidents, from detection and triage through containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review. Coordinate response across Security, SRE, Engineering, Legal, and leadership. Drive decisions under pressure and keep a clear record of actions taken. Communicate incident status, impact, and risk clearly to technical and executive audiences. Participate in and help shape the security on-call rotation. Investigation & Forensics Investigate suspicious activity across cloud infrastructure, containers, identity systems, and application layers using SIEM, Cloud Logging, telemetry, and host and container artifacts. Determine scope, root cause, attacker behavior, and blast radius for confirmed incidents. Quickly assess whether emerging threats (0-days, active exploitation campaigns, bug bounty findings, customer reports) apply to Replit, and whether we're already affected. IR Automation & Tooling Build scripts, automations, and tools (Python, Go, Bash, or directly on Replit) that speed up response, such as automated enrichment, evidence collection, credential and session revocation, workload isolation, and alert triage. Develop and maintain response playbooks and runbooks, and automate them where possible. Integrate response workflows with SIEM, SOAR, ticketing, and chat tooling to cut time-to-contain. Detection & Continuous Improvement Turn incident findings into new or improved detections, logging coverage, and visibility. Lead blameless post-incident reviews and drive remediation items to completion. Run tabletop exercises and simulations to test readiness and find gaps. Required Skills & Experience Proven experience leading or serving as technical lead on security incidents in a cloud or SaaS environment. Strong hands-on investigation skills with SIEM, cloud audit logs, and log-based analysis. Comfortable working through large datasets under time pressure. Solid knowledge of cloud architecture and security, especially Google Cloud Platform (IAM, audit logging, GKE, networking). Working knowledge of Kubernetes and containers, including how to investigate and contain compromised workloads. Understanding of IR frameworks and lifecycle (for example NIST 800-61), plus the vulnerability lifecycle and exploitability analysis. Continuous learning: Passion for staying up to date on new vulnerabilities, exploit trends, and cloud-native security best practices. descriptionAr: About the role Modal’s Inference Runtime team owns the container runtime stack used to run inference and training workloads across our fleet. We work at the boundary of Linux, containers, filesystems, storage, GPU drivers, and distributed systems.Our goal is to make demanding ML workloads start quickly, run efficiently, and remain securely isolated — whether they use a single GPU, hundreds of gigabytes of memory, or multiple GPUs connected with RDMA.We’re looking for a systems engineer who enjoys working deep in the stack. You’ll build production runtime infrastructure in Rust and Go, diagnose difficult Linux and performance problems, and help determine the architecture of Modal’s container platform. You’ll also work closely with maintainers of gVisor and contribute to the runtime itself when the right fix belongs upstream. What you’ll work on Make container startup, checkpoint, and restore dramatically faster for large inference and training workloads. Build multi-GPU and accelerator-aware snapshotting, including efficient handling of GPU memory and RDMA-enabled workloads. Design zero-copy and low-copy data paths between container memory, filesystems, storage, and Modal’s runtime. Optimize large snapshot pipelines using techniques such as parallel uploads, direct I/O, incremental snapshots, and more efficient memory handling. Improve container image and filesystem performance across EROFS, FUSE, page caches, overlay filesystems, and remote storage. Extend our sandboxed runtime to support new GPUs, drivers, profiling tools, and device capabilities across NVIDIA and AMD hardware. Debug complex failures involving system calls, virtual memory, process lifecycle, kernel behavior, GPU drivers, and container isolation. Safely roll out runtime and kernel changes across a heterogeneous fleet using compatibility controls, scheduling constraints, feature flags, and observability. Work across the runtime, scheduler, storage, and GPU infrastructure—and take ambiguous production problems from investigation through deployment. What we’re looking for Strong Linux systems knowledge, particularly processes, virtual memory, filesystems, system calls, scheduling, namespaces, cgroups, and signals. Experience building or debugging container runtimes, sandboxes, Linux kernel, or similarly low-level infrastructure. Strong programming ability in Rust, Go, or another systems language, with an interest in becoming productive in both Rust and Go. Experience profiling and improving systems where memory movement, I/O, synchronization, or kernel interactions dominate performance. Comfort debugging across abstraction boundaries, from application behavior down through runtimes, drivers, and the kernel. An ability to turn loosely defined production problems into well-designed, reliable systems. A desire to own important infrastructure and work closely with both internal teams and customers. Particularly relevant experience Any of the following would be helpful, but none is required: gVisor, runsc , runc , OCI runtimes, seccomp, or checkpoint/restore systems. Linux kernel development, virtualization, sandboxing, kernel modules, or device proxying. CUDA, ROCm, GPU drivers, accelerator virtualization, or GPU profiling. RDMA and high-performance networking. FUSE, EROFS, direct I/O, mmap , page-cache behavior, or storage engines. Large-memory or multi-GPU inference and training systems. Contributions to open-source systems software. Prior gVisor or machine-learning experience is not required. We care more about strong systems fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to learn unfamiliar parts of the stack. Why this role The container runtime is directly on the critical path for inference performance. Improvements here can substantially reduce cold starts, increase token throughput, unlock new accelerator types, and make previously impractical workloads possible.This is an opportunity to work on unusually deep systems problems with immediate production impact. You’ll have room to shape the architecture, contribute to open-source runtime technology, and take ownership of foundational infrastructure used by every inference and training workload on Modal.

descriptionAr: About the Role OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across EMEA by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls. In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for EMEA account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure. You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region. This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking. In this role, you will: Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for EMEA account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes. Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies. Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers. Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines. Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders. Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution. Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information. Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls. Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support. Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools. You might thrive in this role if you have: 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment. Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes. Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability. Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams. Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills. Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales. Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls. A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity. descriptionAr: Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. On the data team, that means building the systems that make our data reliable, understandable, and usable by both humans and AI. We're looking for an analytics engineer or data engineer who wants to build the foundation for an AI-native data organization. You'll design core data models, pipelines, semantic layers, data quality systems, governance practices, and warehouse workflows that power the entire company: helping teams make strategic decisions, operate the business, and move faster with trusted data. You'll also make sure those systems are secure, privacy-aware, and legible to AI agents, data scientists, and the rest of the company. This role is for someone who can operate at the boundary of analytics engineering, data engineering, data governance, and internal product. You care about dimensional modeling, dbt standards, cost-aware warehouse design, access controls, privacy, and the details that make data trustworthy. You also believe AI should make the data stack faster, easier to maintain, and more accessible across the company without weakening security or governance. What You'll Do Build the core data foundation - design and maintain high-quality data models, marts, and pipelines that make analysis fast, reliable, and reusable. Manage the data warehouse - help own warehouse architecture, environments, permissions, performance, cost, data lifecycle, and operational hygiene so the platform scales cleanly. Make the warehouse AI-readable - own the documentation, semantic context, metadata, lineage, and retrieval patterns that AI systems depend on to understand and query Perplexity's data correctly. Own data modeling standards - define and champion dbt patterns, dimensional modeling practices, naming conventions, tests, and review processes. Lead data governance practices - define standards for access, ownership, lineage, documentation, retention, quality, and sensitive data handling across the analytical warehouse. Build with security and privacy in mind - partner with engineering, security, legal, and finance where needed to ensure data access, sharing, and AI-enabled workflows are appropriate and controlled. Automate data quality and maintenance - build AI-assisted workflows that detect issues, explain root causes, suggest fixes, generate tests, and reduce manual firefighting. Improve data team productivity - automate repetitive workflows, improve tooling, streamline development, and make it easier for data scientists and stakeholders to answer questions. Partner across the company - work closely with data scientists, engineering, product, finance, and GTM teams to translate analytical needs into durable data systems. Shape tooling decisions - evaluate build-versus-buy tradeoffs, manage vendor relationships when needed, and choose tools that scale with the team. What We're Looking For 6+ years of experience as an analytics engineer, data engineer, data scientist, or closely related role. Deep SQL expertise - you can reason about correctness, performance, joins, grain, and edge cases in complex warehouse queries. Strong data modeling experience - you've worked hands-on with dbt (or a similar transformation framework) in production, and you understand dimensional modeling, data contracts, testing, and how analytical schemas should evolve. Pipeline ownership - you've built, maintained, debugged, and improved production data pipelines. Warehouse management experience - you've worked with warehouse administration, access patterns, permissions, performance tuning, cost management, or operational ownership. Governance mindset - you think clearly about data ownership, access controls, privacy, retention, lineage, auditability, and the risks of making data too easy to access. AI-native working style - you already use AI to speed up development, documentation, QA, exploration, and repetitive workflow automation. Stakeholder fluency - you know how to turn messy analytical requirements into trusted models, metrics, and reusable data assets. Autonomy and execution - you can take projects from ambiguous problem to production-quality system with minimal oversight. Operational judgment - you care about reliability, governance, security, cost, and long-term maintainability. Bonus Snowflake administration, optimization, cost management, or warehouse performance tuning. Experience with RBAC, PII handling, data classification, retention policies, audit workflows, or privacy/security reviews. Experience with Databricks or other modern data infrastructure. Experience building semantic layers, metrics layers, metadata systems, or data catalogs. Python experience for data tooling, automation, orchestration, or quality checks. Previous experience as an early analytics engineer or data engineer at a high-growth startup. Why This Role Own the foundation - your work will determine how fast and confidently the company can use data. Build for humans and AI - the next generation of data infrastructure needs to be understandable by agents as well as analysts. High leverage - better models, pipelines, and tools multiply every data scientist and every stakeholder who depends on data. Small team, broad scope - you'll have room to define standards, choose tools, and ship systems that become company-wide defaults.

descriptionAr: About Us At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale. With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world. Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater. About the team: We are a small but mighty team of three analytics engineers powering LangChain’s internal data infrastructure and analytics. We’re a full-stack team, meaning we work end-to-end across the data stack, from data ingestion to enabling self-serve agentic analytics. Learn more about what we’ve built so far here ! About the role: We are expanding our data team and looking for a analytics engineer to join us. We build products used by elite companies and over a million developers, and data plays a critical role in sharping our strategies and decision making. In this role you will help lay the foundation for business teams to diagnose issues, uncover opportunities, and drive success using data. If you enjoy building data infrastructure and empowering teams with actionable insights, this role is for you. *Location: SF, NYC, Boston, or Remote U.S. What you will do: Build scaleable dbt models and context that describe our business, powering a self-serve analytics experience Work with and expand on our foundational data stack — Fivetran, dbt, BigQuery, Hex Connect data from a variety of sources (Salesforce, Stripe, Metronome, Postgres, etc) into our BigQuery warehouse Build dashboards that track progress against company goals and KPIs Analyze product usage and operational data to surface insights around customer health, adoption, and revenue Develop and leverage a deep understanding of our business metrics to drive alignment and decision-making What you'll bring: 3+ years experience in a related role (analytics engineer, data engineer, or similar) Technical proficiency in BigQuery, dbt, Hex, Fivetran, Segment (or similar tools) Detail oriented, enjoys data spelunking, and can synthesize findings effectively Curiosity and a strong business sense to help anticipate needs and generate meaningful insights Start up DNA. You thrive in fast-paced and unstructured environments and are energized by finding out what matters most You are self-directed - you don’t wait for process or oversight to start making an impact Compensation & Benefits: We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, meaningful equity, and benefits such as health and dental coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, and life insurance. We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations. Benefits Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

To make that happen, a complex orchestra of IP address configuration and distributed systems need to be in harmony to deliver packets from users, through our edge network and then onwards to our customers origin servers or networks. On the Addressing team, you will architect, program, and maintain core software services that enable large corporate networks to be protected by Cloudflare. Recent projects range from IP conservation efforts, supporting use cases for Policy driven IP address assignment, designing traffic engineering tools that improve the quality of service for billions of users around the world, and building customer APIs to control BGP dynamically. The Addressing team works closely with our system reliability engineers, network engineers  and product engineering teams to build automated systems that span the entire Cloudflare stack. About the role We are looking for talented Software Engineers to join our small but growing team. You will work on a range of microservices written mainly in Go. The ever growing suite of Cloudflare products and services means our addressing tools are always evolving. You will have the opportunity to take on very impactful projects critical for Cloudflare. You will spend time learning the inner workings of our edge routers, servers, DNS and IP provisioning pipelines. You will work closely with other engineers to understand their needs and create scalable platforms to be used across the company. Some of the technologies we use include Go, PostgreSQL, Docker, Kafka, Lua, Clickhouse, SaltStack, Prometheus and the usual Unix/Linux tools and workflows. We strive to build reliable, fault-tolerant systems that can operate at Cloudflare’s scale. We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. AI creates an opportunity to rethink this work: build agentic buying experiences for employees, automate work for approvers and stakeholders, and businesses make better purchasing decisions. Use data and customer research to choose the next iteration. Lead execution with engineers and designers, make scope and sequencing tradeoffs, and align partner teams on dependencies. Work with Sales, Implementation, and Customer Experience to turn customer commitments into repeatable product capabilities and support successful adoption. You can reason about model quality, latency, cost, and user control, and choose where AI improves the experience. You can work with engineers on data models and integrations, use data to investigate problems, and build prototypes to test ideas. Deep customer curiosity and strong design judgment. You can learn unfamiliar purchasing and finance workflows, distinguish recurring needs from one-off requests, and make the product easier to use. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Miami, FL OR Atlanta, GA About the Role: We are seeking an entrepreneurial Sales Director to lead our DN/AI Growth Segment, focusing on both the acquisition and expansion of our fastest-growing Startup accounts. In this role, you will scale a high-performing team tasked with bringing the world’s most innovative AI companies onto Cloudflare's platform. To thrive, you must bring a founder mentality and deep familiarity with the VC ecosystem to capture high-growth startups at inception. You possess a sharp understanding of the dynamics of the hyperscaler market and the AI landscape, allowing you to position Cloudflare as the definitive infrastructure layer for modern workloads. Finally, you are highly familiar with PLG sales motions, knowing exactly how to identify high-potential, self-serve developer accounts and seamlessly transition them into enterprise expansions. Responsibilities: Own and exceed quarterly revenue targets, driving both high-velocity new logo acquisition and strategic account expansion within the AI and startup ecosystem. Recruit, coach, and develop a world-class sales team, instilling a high-tempo, execution-oriented culture tailored to technical buyers. Effectively articulate Cloudflare’s value proposition across our connectivity cloud, including Workers AI, R2 storage, network security, and developer platforms. Partner closely with Product, Growth, and Marketing to seamlessly convert self-serve developer usage into structured enterprise agreements. Act as a key executive sponsor for high-growth startups, founders, and VC partners, positioning Cloudflare as the foundational architecture for the next generation of tech. You might be a good fit if you have: 10+ years of experience in enterprise software sales with at least 3+ leading sales teams A proven track record of leading high-performing sales teams in the cloud infrastructure, SaaS, or developer platform space. A strong understanding of modern application architecture, serverless computing, and how AI startups utilize compute and data storage. Active connections within the tech startup and venture capital ecosystems, with an innate ability to spot and engage high-potential accounts early. Hands-on experience navigating hybrid sales models that blend product-led growth with top-down enterprise execution. A history of thriving in fast-paced, rapidly evolving markets where you can turn ambiguity into clear, actionable sales strategies   What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! You’ll partner with team leads to connect their plans and resolve gaps between roadmaps. You’ll also improve how engineering changes reach teams across Engineering, Product, and Design, along with Documentation and Support. Your goal is a lightweight process giving partners the information and preparation time they need before changes reach customers. You’ll join an early TPM team and help shape how the function works at Sentry. Success means helping teams deliver together through technical judgment, clear communication, and practical coordination. This role is based in San Francisco, with three days per week in the office. What You’ll Do AI Delivery Connect roadmaps across AI/ML, Issues Platform, Product Design, and Ingest into a shared delivery plan. Sequence platform capabilities, product features, and design work so teams address dependencies before they delay a release. Help teams assign accountable owners, resolve open decisions, and communicate commitments. Partner with engineering and product owners to define release readiness, including evaluation results, staged rollouts, eligibility, and access requirements. Bring ingestion and reliability dependencies into roadmap discussions so teams understand the risks behind delivery commitments. Drive risk mitigation with clear owners, contingency plans, and timely escalation. Give teams and leadership an accurate view of progress, dependencies, decisions, and risks. Change Readiness Build a lightweight process for identifying changes affecting other teams, notifying partners, and confirming readiness before release. descriptionAr: About Sentry Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building. Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future. About the Role You’ll own AI-assisted coding within Sentry’s Platform Engineering organization, building the systems and workflows AI coding agents need to contribute reliably to our codebase. Your work will span engineering teams, with Developer Infrastructure as your home base. Your first focus will be making internal developer systems accessible to agents. Many workflows currently depend on human interaction through a UI. You’ll identify the most valuable gaps, expose those capabilities through APIs, and connect tools such as Claude Code to complete development workflows. From there, you’ll improve the quality of AI-generated pull requests and automate recurring engineering work, including dependency upgrades, minor bug fixes, and maintenance. You’ll build the context and execution environment agents need: relevant repository information, tools and permissions, state management, tests, logs, recovery mechanisms, and evaluations. You’ll partner with engineers across Sentry to understand where agents succeed, where they fail, and which changes improve the development process. This role combines technical direction with hands-on implementation, from choosing the problems to solve through building, measuring, and improving the solutions. This role is based in San Francisco, with three days per week in the office to work closely with Platform teams and engineering leadership. What You’ll Do Set priorities for AI-assisted development at Sentry, using engineer feedback and workflow data to identify where agents would provide the most value. Make internal developer systems accessible through APIs and build integrations enabling agents to complete workflows across those systems. Build context systems and agent execution tooling, including tool access, permissions, checkpoints, retries, and logging. Develop automated checks, evaluations, and feedback loops to improve the correctness, maintainability, and review readiness of AI-generated pull requests. Automate recurring work such as security dependency upgrades, minor bug fixes, and routine maintenance. Improve supporting developer workflows, including issue triage and CI/CD, where they limit agent effectiveness or create repetitive work for engineers. Lead changes across engineering teams, build agreement on priorities, and measure whether the tools reduce manual work and improve delivery. How You Work You’ve used AI coding agents on real development work and have informed views on their strengths, limitations, and failure modes. You bring structure to ambiguous problems, choose a practical starting point, and follow through on delivery. You move comfortably between infrastructure, backend systems, and developer tooling. You know when to build, integrate an existing tool, involve another team, or stop work with limited value. You combine data with direct feedback from engineers to assess whether a solution improves their work. You explain technical tradeoffs clearly and build alignment across teams and senior leadership. Qualifications 10+ years of software engineering experience, including hands-on ownership of production systems. Experience building developer tools, infrastructure, or automation used by engineering teams, such as CI/CD systems, internal APIs, code review tooling, or agent workflows. Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agents, with an understanding of how context, tool access, and validation affect their output. Prior machine learning experience is not required. Strong software engineering and system design fundamentals, including experience building reliable integrations across systems. A track record of leading cross-team technical initiatives from problem definition through implementation and adoption. Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical decisions and recommendations to senior engineering leaders. Nice to Have Experience building agent harnesses, context systems, evaluations, or automated pull request workflows. Experience with code review tooling, static analysis, or automated testing. Experience measuring and improving developer experience or engineering productivity. Experience with large-scale distributed systems or monolith decomposition. Public contributions to developer tooling or AI-assisted development projects. The base salary range that Sentry reasonably expects to pay for this position is $220,000 to $400,000 USD, plus an annual performance bonus of up to 15% of base salary. A successful candidate’s actual base salary (or hourly wage) amount will be determined by a variety of relevant factors including, without limitation, the candidate’s work location, education, work and other relevant experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why the Cohere TPM role? As our Generative Machine Learning organization has continued growing, we are looking for more Technical Program Managers to join the team! Great TPMs at Cohere are well-rounded, executing with precision at the tactical level, while partnering with senior leaders and shaping the big picture at a strategic level, and the opportunities are endless in growing the scale and impact of their work. Cohere’s TPMs would often be described as organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic leaders who are adaptable to the needs of the company and the programs they lead. No day will be the same as the one before, and the dynamic high growth environment will be absolutely perfect for anyone excited about solving novel problems, bringing structure to oftentimes chaotic and fast-paced environments, and ambitious about scaling their own impact and growth alongside the company! Please note: While we are remote-first and accept candidates from all over the world, we are highly prioritizing hiring for people who are within 1-2 hours of British Standard Time (BST). Strong preference for candidates that have worked directly in building foundation models. In-depth knowledge of machine learning, particularly when it comes to Natural Language Processing & Large Language Models (LLMs). Bonus points for experience with Multimodal AI. Experience with working in a chaotic, fast paced, low structure environment. We need someone who is pragmatic, can roll up their sleeves when needed, and can function at the tactical and strategic level to do whatever it takes to make Cohere’s models succeed Personal hands-on understanding of the unique challenges of managing projects and programs in the AI/ML development space as opposed to traditional software program management Managed projects & programs requiring a strong general business acumen, such as coordinating with Finance on reporting needs or Policy on regulatory compliance matters — the broader your experience beyond ML technical program management, the better! (optional, but preferred) Have technical experience in a hands-on capacity. We don’t necessarily need someone with hands on experience training models, but you need to feel comfortable sitting in the same rooms with some of the best researchers in the world, working on highly complex, cutting edge ML problems If some of the above - other than the ML TPM experience - doesn’t line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply! If you consider yourself a thoughtful worker, a lifelong learner, and a kind and playful team member, Cohere is the place for you. We welcome applicants of all kinds and are committed to providing both an equal opportunity process and work environment. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the Role We’re looking for an Integrated Marketing Manager to help translate our products, their value propositions, and our broader brand strategy into audience-specific, globally relevant marketing programs. You’ll shape how people discover, understand, adopt, and engage with our products across markets and stages of the customer journey. You’ll connect product narratives, audience insight, cultural context, and business goals into strategies that make advanced technology feel clear, useful, and human. This is a high-impact individual contributor role for a marketer who understands how product marketing, brand strategy, audience research, and international growth work together. You’ll develop segmentation frameworks, lifecycle and go-to-market programs, regional insights, and partnership opportunities; then work across product marketing, growth, creative, partnerships, analytics, and regional teams to bring them to life. Your work will connect launches, product education, customer engagement, and ongoing storytelling into a coherent journey from awareness to advocacy. To us, creativity is a team sport. Ideas get better when you talk them through and build on each other’s thinking. We value curiosity over certainty, kindness over ego, and the ability to balance craft with decisiveness. In this role, you will: Translate complex product capabilities, use cases, and value propositions into clear, differentiated messaging that is relevant to distinct audiences without losing accuracy, nuance, or the product’s ambition. Develop audience segmentation frameworks based on customer needs, behaviors, use cases, regions, industries, and stages of the customer journey. Create audience-specific messaging and campaign strategies for groups such as creators, builders, professionals, students, consumers, and emerging-market users. Lead cross-functional marketing programs end to end for defined audiences or initiatives, with minimal oversight, setting priorities across awareness, acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and advocacy. Lead research efforts including customer interviews, surveys, social listening, competitive analysis, market trends, and behavioral data. Turn research and performance signals into actionable audience personas, messaging frameworks, briefs, campaign recommendations, and market insights. Identify cultural, regional, and language-specific opportunities across global markets, and help adapt global campaigns for local audiences while maintaining a consistent brand voice. Develop go-to-market plans for new campaigns, product features, audience programs, partnerships, and market expansions. Identify partnership opportunities with creators, developers, communities, platforms, industry groups, and other audience ecosystems. Align partners across product marketing, growth, CRM, creative, analytics, partnerships, and regional marketing; resolve tradeoffs and shape creative direction to deliver coordinated customer journeys. Measure campaign and audience performance, using data to improve messaging, segmentation, customer journeys, regional strategies, and future marketing investments. Build reusable campaign processes and playbooks, and coach peers and junior teammates to improve planning, creative collaboration, and execution. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 5–8 years of experience in product marketing, brand marketing, lifecycle marketing, growth marketing, audience strategy, partnerships, or related fields. Bring deep familiarity with AI products, foundation models, generative AI capabilities and limitations, and common user workflows; this is a critical qualification for the role. Have experience translating complex technology and technical product capabilities into clear, compelling, differentiated customer value propositions. Are a strategic thinker who can turn audience insight, cultural context, product strategy, and business goals into a compelling point of view and an actionable marketing system. Can move fluidly between big-picture strategy and hands-on execution: building the framework, writing the brief, launching the program, and reviewing results. Nice to Have: Experience working with creators, developers, communities, partnerships, or other distinct customer segments. Experience working across cultures, regions, or international markets. Experience with experimentation, performance measurement, social listening, and translating signals into strategic recommendations. Experience in consumer technology, emerging products, developer tools, enterprise products, or other fast-changing categories. The team designs and delivers compensation and benefits programs that are competitive, equitable, innovative, and scalable, while balancing global strategy, local market dynamics, employee experience, and long-term sustainability. This role will serve as a key regional partner, helping translate OpenAI’s global Total Rewards strategy into programs and practices that reflect local market needs, regulatory requirements, and the evolving needs of our employees. In this role, you will partner closely with regional leadership, HR Business Partners, Recruiting, People Operations, Finance, Payroll, Legal, and external partners to design, implement, and manage compensation and benefits programs across APAC. You will operate as both a strategic advisor and hands-on practitioner, balancing global consistency with regional flexibility while maintaining a high bar for employee experience and operational excellence. This role is based in Singapore and we use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the Singapore office per week. In this role, you will: Regional Total Rewards Partnership: Serve as a trusted Total Rewards advisor across APAC, providing strategic and practical guidance on compensation, benefits, market practices, and complex employee matters as the region scales. Compensation Strategy & Design: Support the development and evolution of base pay structures, incentive programs, equity frameworks, and other compensation programs to ensure competitiveness, internal consistency, and alignment with OpenAI’s global compensation philosophy. Benefits Execution & Operations: Partner with the International Benefits Lead to support the implementation and ongoing operation of APAC benefits programmes, aligned with agreed priorities and programme designs. Provide regional support for benefits rollouts, vendor coordination, employee communications and operational issue resolution, and surface local insights to inform programme decisions. Market Benchmarking & Insights: Lead compensation and benefits benchmarking and market analysis across APAC, translating external market developments, regulatory changes, and regional practices into thoughtful recommendations. Offer Strategy & Pay Decisions: Partner with Recruiting and HRBPs on offer design, compensation decisions, and approvals, balancing market competitiveness, internal equity, global philosophy, and local market considerations. Program Management & Governance: Support the effective administration and governance of regional Total Rewards programs, ensuring strong controls, data integrity, regulatory compliance, and consistent application of policies and practices. Employee Experience & Communication: Develop clear, thoughtful communications that help employees and leaders understand and navigate Total Rewards programs, including compensation processes, benefits enrollment, and program changes. Operational Excellence & Automation: Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, and scale Total Rewards processes and tools while strengthening data integrity, controls, and the overall operating model. You might thrive in this role if you have: Total Rewards Expertise: 10+ years of experience in compensation, benefits, or broader Total Rewards, with meaningful experience supporting programs across multiple APAC markets. Regional Knowledge: Strong understanding of APAC compensation and benefits practices, market dynamics, and regulatory considerations, with the ability to navigate differences across countries and cultures. Strategic & Analytical Thinking: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex data, market information, and business needs into clear recommendations. Communication & Influence: Excellent communication and presentation skills, with demonstrated ability to advise senior leaders and navigate nuanced Total Rewards discussions across different audiences and markets. Project Management & Execution: Strong organizational and project management capabilities, with the ability to independently manage multiple complex initiatives in a fast-moving environment. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Proven ability to work effectively across HR, Recruiting, Finance, Legal, Payroll, Operations, and business leadership. Operational Mindset: A strong orientation toward scalable processes, automation, data integrity, and continuous improvement, with a willingness to work hands-on through complex problems. Adaptability: Comfort operating in ambiguity and building solutions in an evolving environment where business needs, markets, and organizational structures can change quickly. descriptionAr: About this Role 👋 Hi, I’m Kevin . I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first Data Analytics Manager at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional. You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem. The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company. Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers. Can you identify and hire talented people? We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others? Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work? Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate. Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization? Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists. Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI? AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy. These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members. Your responsibilities as a Data Analytics Manager To understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today. Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company. As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well. Ashby’s Operating Principles place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. That said, as the company matures and more teams optimize their work, demand for data will likely continue to grow. You will help us meet that demand with good judgment. Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply At Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well. You could be a strong fit if you: Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome. Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion. Are a strong visual and written communicator. You care about clear tables and charts, meaningful labels and definitions, coherent narratives, and making complex work understandable without overstating certainty. Have deep hands-on SQL experience, plus working fluency with dbt-style data modeling, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools. You do not need to have owned

descriptionAr: Overview The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices. We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us. We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand. As our Global Workplace Business Operations Lead, you will manage the business operations and cross-functional program delivery that enable our global Workplace Experience team to scale. In collaboration with the Head of Workplace Experience, you will set the operating framework for your areas, make decisions within agreed priorities and approval limits, and remain hands-on in delivering results. You will own the effectiveness of portfolio operating processes and internal project delivery. What You’ll Do Own the Workplace operating framework: Lead annual and quarterly planning for your areas, translate team strategy into priorities and resource plans, and establish clear decision rights, delivery commitments and measures of success. Resolve sequencing and capacity trade-offs within agreed parameters and recommend when to add people, vendors or technology. Lead internal capital-project delivery: Take accountability for integrated delivery plans across office openings, refreshes and other capital initiatives. Direct the work of external PMs within agreed scopes, align internal workstreams, resolve delivery issues and hold partners accountable for schedule, cost, quality and operational readiness. Own portfolio controls and insight: Establish dependable lease administration, obligation tracking, space and occupancy information, and portfolio reporting. Set data and control standards, ensure actions have owners, and turn trends and risks into recommendations before deadlines or capacity constraints become problems. Drive financial planning and performance: Own the processes and quality of operating and capital forecasts, commitments, actuals and variance analysis in partnership with Finance. Challenge assumptions, recommend corrective actions and investment trade-offs, and give the Head of Workplace Experience a reliable basis for budget and commitment decisions. Set the systems and reporting roadmap: Own business requirements, governance and improvement priorities for workplace tools such as Envoy. Establish useful performance measures, improve data quality, and automate repeatable work while maintaining appropriate controls and keeping processes practical for the team. Lead EHS program governance: Establish a risk-based plan, clear responsibilities and a review cadence with qualified vendors and internal teams. Drive follow-through on assessed obligations and remediation across offices and remote populations, maintain evidence of completion, and escalate material risks without substituting for specialist advice. Set standards for delivery and handover: Own the development and use of project playbooks, planning processes and operational-readiness criteria. Bring together design standards and occupancy requirements, and ensure completed projects transfer to local operations with the documentation, training, vendor arrangements and issue ownership needed to run well. Serve as a senior operating partner: Lead cross-functional operating and project reviews, surface decisions with clear recommendations, and represent your areas with internal and external partners. Drive resolution within your authority, escalate material changes with options, and build accountability without adding unnecessary layers. What You Bring Senior functional leadership: 8+ years in workplace business operations, corporate real estate, facilities programs or a closely related field, with increasing responsibility for complex, multi-site programs and their outcomes. You have operated with substantial autonomy, not only administered plans set by others. Project and program management expertise: You are a project manager at the core. You are quick and agile, but methodical when it comes to planning for, organizing, tracking, and executing on a project in a way that keeps everything and everyone aligned and on task. Relevant delivery depth: You have a record of delivering office buildouts, relocations or capital improvements as an internal owner, with accountability for scope, financial performance, schedules, change control and external delivery partners. Strong financial and analytical judgment: You have experience driving forecasting and reporting processes, challenging assumptions and translating portfolio data into resource or investment recommendations; strong spreadsheet and analytical skills. Experience building an operating framework: You have established planning, governance, performance measures and systems that helped a growing function deliver more predictably. You know when structure improves execution and when it becomes unnecessary process. Leadership across organizational boundaries: You can secure commitments, challenge constructively and resolve competing priorities across teams and vendors. You communicate risks and recommendations credibly to senior leaders and know which decisions to make independently and which to escalate. Hands-on ownership and sound judgment: You can move between portfolio-level trade-offs and project details, deliver through others without losing accountability, handle sensitive information responsibly, and maintain a kind, service-oriented approach under pressure. Helpful, not required: International portfolio experience, workplace technology ownership, EHS program governance, or a relevant project-management credential.

descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises. About the Role The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support. We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution. Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements. In this role, you will: Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents. Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation. Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers. Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through. Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners. Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams. Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes. Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates. Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations. Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed. Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure. Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments. Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation. Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally. You might thrive in this role if you: Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues. Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations. Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses. Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis
