descriptionAr: About This Role Hi, I’m Casey, Head Customer Success Management and Customer Education at Ashby. I’m thrilled to be hiring our first EMEA-based Recruiting Operations Consultant to support Strategic, Mid-Market, and Startup customers in the EMEA region. In this role, you’ll be part of the Customer Education team, blending 1:1 customer consulting, CSM enablement, and educational content creation to scale advanced recruiting operations expertise, strengthen CSM RecOps literacy, and help customers achieve measurable recruiting outcomes. You’ll also collaborate with Professional Services to scope and deliver paid consulting engagements (SOWs), helping shape and evolve offerings such as Process Optimization and Fractional RecOps — and, when needed, building reports or processes on behalf of customers to support their goals. Day-to-day, this looks like: Delivering high-impact consulting via RecOps Connects (complimentary 1:1 engagements) and paid engagements, focused on recruiting strategy, analytics interpretation, and operational best practices. Partnering with AEs, CSMs, and Professional Services to scope, sell, and deliver paid consulting engagements using the RecOps SOW framework. Translating 1:1 consulting insights into scalable education — Academy courses, guides, webinars, and segment-specific playbooks — that go beyond “how” to explain “why.” Contributing to advanced product education (e.g., interpreting Quality of Hire dashboards, building analytics strategies) and shaping our most sophisticated Customer Education offerings. Partnering closely with the Product Team to distill your observations into tangible feedback. Enabling CSMs on foundational RecOps strategies and tactics. You Could Be a Great Fit If You have hands-on experience with Ashby’s product and are excited by the power it offers Talent Acquisition teams. You love helping customers learn — supporting them as they grow into power users. You are an excellent communicator, skilled at clear and concise facilitation. You can navigate a range of stakeholders (e.g., Heads of Talent vs. recruiters) and help them align on shared goals. You’re comfortable working across a spectrum of complexity — from solving simple interview plan questions to building advanced Quality of Hire reporting strategies. You excel at holding stakeholders accountable, setting clear expectations, and facilitating alignment. You are proactive about defining boundaries — enabling CSMs to own foundational RecOps work so you can focus on high-leverage contributions. You are skilled at enabling others, whether in 1:1 sessions or group settings. You have deep empathy for customers and can translate their feedback into actionable insights that shape internal priorities and product direction. You have 2+ years experience in recruiting operations, analytics, and process design — and enjoy helping others level up in these areas. You Might Not Be a Great Fit If: You prefer rigid structure and are uncomfortable with ambiguity or evolving priorities. You don’t enjoy hands-on building with customers, as this role is a mix of both consulting engagements and build-for-me engagements. You are not comfortable running projects from beginning to end, including scoping, execution, and follow-through You want to focus exclusively on individual customer conversations and not contribute to scaled education or internal enablement. You hesitate to hold customers or internal teams accountable, or avoid facilitating alignment when competing opinions are presented. You find it difficult to set boundaries and tend to default to saying “yes” to all requests. Interview Process: Recruiter Screen with Talent Acquisition Team - 30 minutes Hiring Manager Interview - 45 minutes Take Home / Mock Call - 45 minutes Final Panel: Interview with CSM Leadership - 30 min Interview with CS Senior Leadership - 30 minutes Benefits: Competitive salary and equity. Opportunity to work with a talented and passionate team. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it! Generous family paid family leave. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities. Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

You’ll help support Public Sector overall, with a clear focus on Healthcare and SLED, and you’ll collaborate across adjacent verticals where motions overlap (including Life Sciences events). We are looking for a high-energy, revenue-minded marketing strategist who can alternate between strategic pipeline and account planning with vertical sales and flawless execution of industry experiences for customer executives. If you are obsessed with driving pipeline from high-touch, standout programs and are a self-starter who thrives at the intersection of technical innovation, healthcare / public-sector narrative, and enterprise GTM, we want you. This is a remote role with travel for industry programs and customer engagements. What You’ll Do Pipeline Architecture & Vertical Ownership Own the Healthcare / SLED GTM: Build and execute a data-driven marketing plan for Healthcare and SLED, and orchestrate core business partners into one motion aimed at must-win accounts. Master the Land & Expand: Own the vertical pipeline target. Design and run the programs that help priority accounts land, expand, and adopt more of the platform, focused where the commercial opportunity is highest. Creative Agility: Fearlessly think outside the standard playbook to deploy memorable in-person, virtual, and next-gen experiences — and the operational workflows that bring them to life. Industry Narrative: Translate the Cursor (now part of SpaceXAI) mission into healthcare and SLED language — the problems these buyers already feel (clinical / payer / provider / state & education IT), the outcomes they are measured on, and why this platform is the answer. Partner with PMM and corporate marketing so the story stays sharp, consistent, and specific enough that a CIO, CMIO, or public-sector technology leader hears their world, not a generic AI pitch. Sales Partner: Act as the strategic marketing partner to Healthcare and SLED sales. Lead planning calls, provide account-level insights, analyze vertical pipeline trends, lock alignment on priority accounts, and maximize the impact of every motion. Know what you run as Vertical vs what you plug into Enterprise Field formats. Support broader Public Sector needs as needed. Measurement & Operational Excellence Event Orchestration: Obsess over the end-to-end details of every program — ideation, promotion, vendor management, onsite, and follow-up — going beyond day-of execution. Data-Driven Iteration: Track every dollar spent against pipeline generated. Manage your vertical budget toward high-impact investments on critical accounts. Feedback Loop: Serve as the eyes and ears of Healthcare and SLED. Feed Corporate and PMM real-time feedback on messaging resonance and competitive shifts. Your DNA The Healthcare Vertical Owner: You assemble Sales, PMM, Enterprise Field, FE/Solutions, and CS/ADM into one motion aimed at pipeline on the company’s largest accounts, not just events. 5–7+ years of healthcare marketing / GTM experience is required (provider, payer, health systems, health tech, or adjacent). descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI's Vendor Security team helps internal teams work securely with external products, services, and partners. Our work spans software, infrastructure, hardware, professional and managed services, vendor-provided workforces, data, and research. We build the programs and products that help teams understand vendor risk and put effective safeguards in place, protecting our customers, employees, and the company. About the Role We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work. You will independently lead vendor-security engagements: understand the business need, investigate the actual data and access, recommend a practical path, and work with the responsible owners until the safeguards are verified. You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead. This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. You should be comfortable taking a position, explaining the tradeoff, and changing your mind when the evidence changes. Success means internal teams can use vendors securely, reuse work that still applies, and understand what needs to happen next. In this role, you will: Own vendor security engagements from understanding the business need through scoping, assessment, decision, treatment, and reassessment when material facts change. Make assessment decisions independently and use judgment about when to involve peers, specialists, or leadership. Route formal exceptions and risk acceptance to the appropriate decision owners. Understand vendor use cases, workflows, user journeys, data flows, identities, access, integrations, and supply-chain dependencies. Identify plausible attack paths and their consequences for OpenAI. Assess relevant architectures, configurations, controls, logs, and operational practices. Test whether the evidence supports the security claims that matter to the engagement, and make gaps and uncertainty clear. Develop practical treatments, including changes to the operating model, data exposure, access, architecture, vendor choice, controls, or containment. Drive implementation with the responsible owners and verify that the treatment works. Build reusable security patterns with clear applicability, safeguards, evidence requirements, exceptions, and review triggers. Work with Legal, Procurement, and vendors on security addenda. Evaluate proposed terms and deviations against the engagement, explain their security implications, and develop workable positions with the appropriate decision owners. Legal leads wording and negotiation. Learn from internal customers, agree priorities with the Vendor Security lead, and define the requirements, roadmap, and success measures for the bounded programs, products, and services you own. Use Codex or comparable AI-assisted tools to build, inspect, test, and maintain practical improvements to scoping, evidence checks, routing, decision reuse, or treatment tracking. Investigate failures and own the result through adoption, continued operation, and explicit handoff or retirement. Lead delivery across Security and partner teams. Translate goals into technical requirements, milestones, and delivery plans; influence implementation choices; identify systemic risks; resolve dependencies and disagreements; and carry commitments through completion. Use casework, incidents, threat information, and customer feedback to improve decisions and the program. As priorities change, recommend what to do next and explain the tradeoffs and effects on existing commitments. You might thrive in this role if you: Have independently assessed consequential third-party, supply-chain, or comparable security risks, and can apply that judgment to unfamiliar vendor technologies and operating models. Understand security principles and controls, including data protection, access management, application security, prevention, detection, and response. Can reason about architecture, identity, APIs, data flows, logging, integrations, and whether controls work. Know relevant frameworks and standards, including ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, and SOC 2, and can use them to inform an assessment of the actual engagement. Have translated security findings and requirements into practical contractual positions with Legal, Procurement, and vendor representatives. Have delivered useful products or workflow improvements, tested expected behavior and failure cases, learned from users, and owned performance after launch. Can use Codex or comparable AI-assisted development tools to build, run, inspect, and test working solutions. Have independently delivered cross-functional programs, turned ambiguity into technical requirements and plans, and adapted priorities to achieve measurable outcomes. Can judge when to build, use existing systems, or engage partners to resolve blockers. Build constructive relationships with Security, Engineering, Product, Privacy, Legal, business teams, and vendors. Communicate complex security issues clearly in writing and conversation, including your recommendation, supporting evidence, and relevant tradeoffs. Question assumptions, try thoughtful new approaches, investigate unfamiliar systems, and revise your judgment when new evidence changes the situation. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Austin,TX and Washington, D.C. Role Summary Cloudforce One is Cloudflare’s threat operations and research team, responsible for identifying and disrupting cyber threats ranging from sophisticated cyber criminal activity to nation-state sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs).  Cloudforce One works in close partnership with external organizations and internal Cloudflare teams, continuously developing operational tradecraft and expanding ever-growing sources of threat intelligence to enable expedited threat hunting and remediation.  Members of Cloudforce One are at the helm of leveraging an incredibly vast and varied set of data points that only one of the world’s largest global networks can provide.  The team is able to analyze these unique data points, at massive scale and efficiency, synthesizing findings into actionable threat intelligence to better protect our customers. As a Software Engineer on this team, you build and evolve systems that help security practitioners assess technical risk, investigate complex systems, prioritize issues, and deliver actionable guidance to engineering teams. You will be responsible for translating complex security requirements and investigative methods into robust, scalable, and high-performance applications that have a direct impact on making the internet better, safer, and more powerful every day. Role Responsibilities While the majority of our services are now written in Go and TypeScript, you will also work with technologies such as Rust, Kafka, Redis, Kubernetes, Terraform, and PostgreSQL. We also pride ourselves in dogfooding our own products and services so you will be extensively working with Cloudflare’s developer platform as well. We are looking for great engineers regardless of experience with any of these specific technologies. Responsibilities include: Design, build, run, and scale distributed tools and services that translate security tradecraft into scalable, evidence-based systems and workflows. Partner with security practitioners to understand workflows, bottlenecks, and opportunities for automation. Improve system design and architecture to ensure stability, performance, and maintainability of both internal and customer-facing services. Analyze, communicate, and help prioritize complex technical concepts across teams. Mentor and guide other developers in the team, helping to build collective technical expertise and promote best practices for writing well-tested, modular, and reusable code. This role may require flexibility to be on-call outside of standard working hours to address technical issues as needed. Desirable Skills and Experience Working knowledge of cybersecurity concepts such as threat modeling, attack techniques, trust boundaries, exploitability, and defensive controls Familiarity with incident response workflows, network containment, and remediation Practical experience in vulnerability research/exploit development and translating findings into actionable mitigations Experience with AI-assisted development and designing agentic AI workflows At least 5 years of experience building large-scale software applications, preferably distributed systems Experience designing and integrating RESTful APIs and/or gRPC services Knowledge of SQL and common relational database systems such as PostgreSQL Ability to independently define and deliver solutions in ambiguous problem spaces Prior experience writing production-ready code in Go and/or TypeScript Excellent debugging and optimization skills Expertise in writing well-tested code Interest in opportunities to be a technical mentor for teammates Bonus/Nice-to-Have Skills Application security, security research, or security automation experience Deep understanding of DNS, TLS/SSL and HTTP Experience evaluating probabilistic systems Compensation Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location. For Washington D.C. based hires: Estimated annual salary of $150,000 - $206,000 Equity This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI Finance helps ensure the organisation is positioned for long-term success as we pursue our mission. The Strategic Sourcing & Procurement team helps OpenAI scale responsibly and at speed by choosing the right external partners, structuring strong commercial agreements and building resilient supplier relationships. We partner with teams across the company to turn rapidly evolving needs into practical, economically sound solutions. Our sourcing team helps business leaders define the outcomes they need, select capable partners and establish clear commercial and delivery accountability. About the Role We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing Leader to lead and develop the Professional Services sourcing team and set direction across its portfolio. This is a people-management role with accountability for team performance, commercial quality, stakeholder experience and sustained business outcomes. You will translate business priorities into category strategies, achievable delivery plans and clear decision authority, while developing the judgement and independence of experienced sourcing professionals. You will oversee a broad portfolio, from strategic advisory relationships and enterprise programmes to a high volume of statements of work and renewals. You will remain hands-on in selected complex negotiations and critical decisions, while enabling the team to own and deliver its work. Working with senior leaders across Finance, Accounting, Legal, People, Extended Workforce and the business, you will create clarity from incomplete information, resolve competing priorities and adapt the team's approach as OpenAI grows. In this role, you will: Lead and develop the team: set clear objectives and expectations, delegate with appropriate decision boundaries, provide regular feedback, review performance and address persistent gaps. Build development and coverage plans that strengthen capability and reduce reliance on individual experts. Set the Professional Services portfolio strategy and roadmap, connecting business objectives, demand, spend, supplier markets and risk. Guide category plans and decisions on where to compete, consolidate, retain specialist partners or change the service delivery model. Manage the team's pipeline and capacity across strategic negotiations, supplier governance and recurring SOWs. Allocate work by capability, complexity and risk; make resource constraints and dependencies visible; and agree priorities and recovery plans before commitments become unachievable. Personally lead selected critical negotiations and set standards for commercial quality across the team. Review strategy and assumptions early, using credible alternatives and comparable economics to shape scope, resource mix, pricing, deliverables, acceptance criteria, change controls, audit rights and exit protections. Build proportionate intake, tiering, preferred-partner models, playbooks and review pathways with Procurement Operations, Contract Management, Enablement and control functions. Agree decision rights and usable handovers so repeatable work moves efficiently and material exceptions receive the right attention. Strengthen supplier relationships and accountability through segmentation, competition, performance reviews and improvement plans. Agree post-signature owners with the business and use service evidence, concentration risk, renewal exposure and transition options to guide supplier decisions. Assess supplier productivity proposals for their effect on staffing, fees, quality and delivery risk. Partner with Finance and Accounting on spend visibility, demand scenarios, forecasting, approval discipline and invoice-to-contract alignment. Test fee models, staffing assumptions, change exposure and total economics, with clear baselines for savings, cost avoidance and realized value. Partner with Legal, People and Extended Workforce to select appropriate service models and distinguish Professional Services from contingent labour or hiring needs. Translate specialist guidance into practical safeguards for service delivery, intellectual property, confidentiality and workforce-related risk. Establish a concise view of portfolio and team performance covering commercial and service outcomes, pipeline health, cycle time, risk, stakeholder experience and team capability. Use evidence to improve decisions, commitments and delivery; distinguish negotiated benefits from value realized. Build trusted senior stakeholder relationships and challenge demand, scope or supplier preferences constructively. Resolve difficult trade-offs on value, speed, quality and risk, and escalate decisions beyond your authority with clear options and a recommendation. Personally use approved AI tools and lead adoption of improved sourcing workflows across the team, including supplier research, proposal analysis, negotiation preparation and reporting. Validate sources and calculations, retain human commercial judgement, and measure adoption and gains in quality, speed or capacity. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 10+ years of progressive strategic sourcing, procurement or category management experience, with substantial depth across multiple Professional Services categories and ownership from strategy through supplier performance. Bring 5+ years of people leadership experience, including formal responsibility for objectives, performance, development and delegation. Can demonstrate stronger team capability, independent judgement and sustained delivery through your leadership. Have personally led complex services negotiations and can explain the alternatives, commercial decisions

Browser Run is the centre of that work, and it is the product this role owns. It runs full browser sessions on Cloudflare’s global network and lets developers drive them with code or with an agent: a Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint that any Puppeteer, Playwright or CDP client can connect to from anywhere, Workers bindings, and a REST API for the common jobs — screenshots, PDFs, Markdown extraction, scraping and crawling. Available Locations: Austin About the Role The CNI team builds and operates the systems that let Cloudflare's enterprise customers connect their networks directly to Cloudflare through private, dedicated interconnects — rather than traversing the public Internet. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience 3+ years experience as an Engineering Manager for a team of Software and Systems Engineers. Knowledge of GRE, VXLAN, or other overlay/tunnel technologies. Systems-level programming experience in Go, Python, Rust, C, or C++. Comfort with customer-facing technical communication (escalation handling, partner engagements). Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools (e.g., code completion, codebase analysis, log/data exploration) in a professional setting. An overview of this role As a Strategic Account Executive, you will own a portfolio of our largest most strategic customers and prospects in Germany, helping them get the most value from GitLab’s AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You’ll break into net new enterprise accounts and expand GitLab’s footprint within existing customers, using a consultative approach to understand their business needs and guide successful adoption and expansion of GitLab. You’ll work closely with pre- and post-sales teams and strategic channel partners to drive full-cycle sales, from prospecting and qualification through rollout, usage, and long-term growth, while acting as the voice of your customers by feeding their feedback and product ideas into GitLab’s public issue tracker. Leverage solution selling expertise to respond efficiently to customer needs and identify business potential in order to build a strategic, long-term partnership with your customers. Has a deep understanding of the customer, including an understanding of their performance metrics and develops plans in anticipation of the customer’s business strategies and goals. Expand knowledge of industry as well as the competitive posture of the company Contribute to root cause analysis on wins/losses. Communicate lessons learned to the team, including account managers, the marketing team, and the technical team Provide account leadership and direction in the pre- and post-sales process Conduct sales activities including prospecting and developing opportunities in Strategic accounts Ensure the successful rollout and adoption of GitLab products through strong account management activities and coordination with pre-and-post sales engineering and support resources Utilize a consultative approach, discuss business issues with prospect and develop a formal quote, a written sales proposal or a formal sales presentation addressing their business needs. Develop an account plan to sell to customers based on their business needs. Requirements Experience selling into highly complex organizations Demonstrated consistent results and overachievement of quota Excellent communication and presentation skills; comfortable presenting to C-Level executives. Experience with solutions selling and positioning value to customers based on their needs. An overview of this role As Senior Renewals Operations Manager at GitLab, you'll help own the operational engine that makes renewals predictable, measurable, and efficient at scale. Reporting to the Director of CX Operations, you'll be the Renewals team's go-to business partner for processes, tooling, forecasting and insights, consumption and subscription data, and the steps required to quote and close a renewal. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. You'll lead through ownership and influence, connecting teams and workflows, turning ambiguous problems into clear next steps, and driving improvements that others across the revenue organization depend on. What you'll do Own and continuously improve the end-to-end renewal operating model; from renewal identification, assignment through risk management, quoting, through to close and post-renewal data hygiene processes. Develop and improve the operating cadences that guide the renewal business, with a focus on efficiency and process improvement. Define, maintain, and evolve retention reporting with cross-functional partners, including gross and net retention, churn and downgrade analysis, and the drivers behind each. Partner with Revenue Technology, Revenue Analytics, Finance, and other stakeholders to improve Salesforce and the systems and data flows supporting customer relationship management (CRM), subscription and entitlement records, quoting, orders, billing, and reporting. Translate business needs into requirements, validate solutions, and strengthen data quality and operational controls. Simplify and scale the renewal motion through automation, standardized workflows, alerts, playbooks, and self-service insights that reduce manual effort and improve execution consistency. Support renewals planning and capacity management, including segmentation implementation, coverage models, productivity assumptions, capacity modeling, supporting target setting, and scenario planning. Own and mature the Renewal Operations case-management program, including intake, triage, routing, service-level visibility, resolution, and root-cause analysis. Requests may include user migrations, de-duplication, Renewal Manager ownership changes, compensation exceptions, and Salesforce or data issues. Raise the operating standard in your domain by documenting processes, mentoring others on how the renewal motion works, and contributing to broader Revenue Operations initiatives that need the renewals perspective. What you'll bring Experience in Renewals Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, management consulting, strategy, or a similar analytical and problem-solving role, with ownership of operational improvements and cross-functional initiatives. Hands-on experience with both consumption and subscription renewal motions, including renewal forecasting, retention reporting, and the contractual and process mechanics that govern how renewals close. Strong critical thinking and structured problem-solving skills. You can break down ambiguous problems into clear workstreams and move them forward. Strong quantitative and analytical skills. You're highly proficient in Excel or Google Sheets, can build and validate models from scratch, and can translate analysis into clear recommendations and action. Experience with Structured Query Language (SQL) or equivalent data-querying tools is preferred, not required. Systems thinking and experience using Salesforce for pipeline and renewals reporting. You understand how changes in one part of the go-to-market motion affect others, including how CRM, subscription or entitlement records, quoting, and billing relate to one another, and you design solutions accordingly. Sound commercial judgment and an understanding of renewal complexity, including co-terming, amendments, expansions, downgrades, price changes, multiyear agreements, auto-renewals, procurement requirements, and approval policies. Strong cross-functional collaboration skills. You build trust with stakeholders at all levels, including field teams and senior leadership, and influence without direct authority. Curiosity, sound judgment, and a bias toward action. You learn new domains and tools quickly, move from insight to implementation, and follow through until improvements are adopted and sustained.
